evidence: Parent Context: 'families arrive as three-ticket instalments (sidecar keying x3, git_adapter by-path loads x3, nested-pytest --basetemp x3, comment key/send fit x5, compaction x6)'

findings.finding: Parent AC1 inventories five duplicated-computation families and requires each be 'delivered by one consolidation child', but the family 'git_adapter by-path loads x3' is covered by NO child in the complete roster. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that every child adding tests/ files must satisfy PLW1510/PT and the 20s timeout budget once 73b8 lands (or sequence 73b8 last), so 73b8's make-lint AC is not re-broken by siblings.
evidence: 73b8 AC: 'ruff check with PLW1510 and PT selected reports zero findings on main; checked by make lint' and Scope 'tests/** (backlog fixes for PLW1510/PT ...)'.

Parent dep manifest lists many new test files as absent: tests/unit/store/test_stamped_lock.py, test_store_paths.py, test_git_outcome.py, test_merge_recovery.py, tests/_nested_pytest.py, test_content_triggers.py, test_finding_carry_forward.py, etc.

Consumer worklist of the tests/** lint budget: every child adding a new test file (1cf6,3436,4329,44ff,4cee,6f18,7931,7e0d,825c,d6e3,da84,111a,2e0f,4144,7f54,77e7,fcb7) — each must satisfy PLW1510/PT and the 20s timeout after 73b8 lands.
findings.finding: Consumer-impact / scope overlap: child 73b8 (bold, hardening) sweeps all of tests/** to clear the PLW1510 + PT backlog and add timeout marks, while eleven other children each ADD new test files under tests/ (many named in the parent's dep list as 'absent'); 73b8 does not scope those not-yet-created files and the new tests must themselves be PT/PLW1510-clean or 73b8's zero-findings AC breaks.
scenarios: 73b8 lands and clears the backlog to zero; a later consolidation child adds a new test file with a subprocess.run lacking check= or a PT-style violation, re-introducing a lint finding and breaking the make-lint AC that 73b8's close depended on; or a new nested-pytest helper test (25b4) trips the 20s budget without a marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Sequence 73b8 to land after the tests-adding children, or add a note to each test-adding child that new test files must be PT/PLW1510-clean and marker-annotate any >20s test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the title with the body: either broaden the headline to name the two remits (collapse duplicates AND close the process gaps the defect review found) or add a one-line scope note under Context that the epic carries both a consolidation class and a behaviour-adding hardening class.
evidence: Title: 'Collapse duplicated logic into shared modules (fortnight defect review)'
AC: 'The hardening children ... deliberately ADD behaviour and lines, so the two consolidation guarantees do not apply to them'

9 hardening children named: dormant-fibre-pterosaurs, tireless-ruinable-prairiedog, bold-abeyant-indri, amenable-befuddling-phoenix, nitro-zombie-mealworm, diabetic-inorganic-equine, emulsible-beneficent-caiman, compliable-evaluable-mamba, tectonic-toxophilic-limpet
findings.finding: The title promises only consolidation ('Collapse duplicated logic into shared modules'), but nine of the 23 children are 'hardening children' that the plan itself says 'deliberately ADD behaviour and lines' — a scope the headline does not signal. A reader scanning only the title would not expect roughly a third of the work to add new behaviour (test-hygiene tooling, escalation gates, route replay blocking, caused_by validation).
findings.location: Title and Acceptance Criteria ('two child classes with different guarantees')
scenarios: A reviewer or downstream consumer treats the epic as pure refactoring (net-negative lines, no behaviour change) and is surprised when hardening children introduce new gates/thresholds and added lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to something like 'Address the fortnight defect review: collapse duplicated logic and close its process gaps', or add a Context sentence stating the epic has two remits.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For any duplication family whose copies live outside `src/rebar` (e.g. the named --basetemp x3 family spanning scripts/mutation_gate.py and .github/workflows/*.yml), extend that child's uniqueness-guard scan root to the trees the family actually inhabits (src + scripts + .github/workflows, as scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py already does), or state per child which tree its guard scans and why that covers every copy.
evidence: Plan names family 'nested-pytest --basetemp x3'

search_files: scripts/mutation_gate.py:440,577 build '--basetemp=' argv; .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:659, test.yml:145, external-integration.yml (x5), structured-output-baseline.yml:118 all carry --basetemp lines

The reference guard test_spawn_detached scans only _proc.__file__.parent (src/rebar), whereas scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py scans PY_SCAN_TREES=('src','scripts') plus .github/workflows — the plan adopts the former, narrower scan root while claiming families whose blast radius spans workflows/scripts
Guard-construction step 5 says 'The guard proves uniqueness only' — but a uniqueness proof scoped to src/rebar is silent about copies in the two other trees the family actually inhabits
findings.finding: The Guard-test construction rule step 1 confines the uniqueness scan to `src/rebar`, but at least one named duplication family — 'nested-pytest --basetemp x3' — has its copies OUTSIDE src/rebar (scripts/mutation_gate.py and several .github/workflows/*.yml), which the plan's own Scope section lists. A guard that scans only src/rebar cannot detect a --basetemp copy re-entering via a script or workflow, so the uniqueness guarantee is unenforced for cross-tree families.
findings.location: Guard-test construction rule, step 1 ('Scan every file under `src/rebar` EXCEPT the owner module'); cross-check Scope ('.github/workflows/', 'scripts' helpers)
scenarios: A future edit reintroduces a hand-rolled --basetemp computation in a new workflow YAML or in scripts/, and the src/rebar-only guard passes green while the duplication the epic set out to eliminate has silently re-entered
The --basetemp consolidation child collapses the src/rebar copies but leaves the scripts/workflow copies, and its uniqueness test still passes because it never looks there
findings.suggested_fix: Amend Guard-test construction rule step 1 to: 'Scan every file across the trees the construct inhabits (default src/rebar; widen to scripts/ and .github/workflows/ for families whose copies the review located there, as scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py does) EXCEPT the owner module.' Have each cross-tree child name its scan roots explicitly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record an explicit ordering (d6e3 before da84) or a depends_on edge so merge_recovery consumes the shared classifier rather than forking the predicates.
evidence: da84 Approach: 'abort classification (via the git outcome classifier if landed, else the existing predicates)'.
Parent Approach: 'order by blast radius (store paths and stamped lock first, merge recovery last)' — names da84 last but not d6e3's position.
da84's roster deps show no depends_on d6e3; d6e3 is not sequenced relative to da84.
findings.finding: Dependency gap: child da84 (merge_recovery) conditionally consumes child d6e3's git-outcome classifier ('via the git outcome classifier if landed, else the existing predicates') but the roster records no dependency edge and the parent's only ordering statement ('merge recovery last') does not pin d6e3 before da84.
scenarios: da84 lands before d6e3; da84 duplicates the abort-classification predicates it would otherwise have reused, then d6e3 later has a second classifier copy to fold — recreating the duplication the epic exists to remove and potentially tripping d6e3's own uniqueness guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Add depends_on d6e3 to da84 (or state in da84 that it lands after d6e3) so the 'if landed' branch is guaranteed.
